Examining `validateFilter` in `shortcut_service.go` to locate the filter parsing logic.
Reading the remainder of `validateFilter` to trace the filter parsing logic.

The filter expression is parsed by CEL via `cel-go` (github.com/google/cel-go/cel). The engine lives in the internal/filter package.

`internal/filter/engine.go` creates the CEL environment from the schema and compiles filter strings. `internal/filter/parser.go` converts the CEL AST into an internal Condition IR. `internal/filter/render.go` renders that IR into dialect-specific SQL via `Program.Render` with a `DialectName`. `internal/filter/schema.go` defines the memo field schema and CEL environment options. `internal/filter/ir.go` holds the IR type definitions.

Each dialect driver in `store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/memo.go` calls `filter.AppendConditions` with its `DialectName`. `render.go` switches on that name to emit dialect-specific SQL constructs such as JSON functions, parameter placeholders, and date extraction functions.

q25. **CEL** (via `github.com/google/cel-go/cel`) in `internal/filter/` (`engine.go`, `parser.go`, `render.go`, `schema.go`); `ListMemosRequest.filter` is documented as a CEL expression in `proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`, validated in `server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go` (`validateFilter`), and at query time `store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/memo.go` calls `filter.AppendConditions`, which uses `Engine.CompileToStatement` to compile the string with cel-go, lower the CEL AST to a dialect-agnostic `Condition` IR in `parser.go`, and walk that IR in `render.go` with the active `DialectName` to emit dialect-specific SQL (e.g. `?` vs `$n`, `JSON_EXTRACT`/`jsonb`, `strftime`/`EXTRACT`/`DAYOFMONTH`) plus bound args appended to the WHERE clause.
